transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-11-01, 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Latitude Head of AI), Mariana Lopez (Platform Engineer), Tom Grey (CTO)

[00:00] Ava: hey everyone, thanks for joining our QBR, we wanted to go over usage, costs, reliability, and roadmap alignment before the holiday spike. quick round robin?
[00:12] Raj: yep, thanks Ava. uh we've been ramping up checkout personalization, about a 2.5x increase in inference calls since last quarter. costs are up and we're seeing tail latency on some of the 2k token flows.
[00:25] Diego: okay can you describe the tail? is it specific to certain endpoints or payload sizes?
[00:30] Mariana: mostly the long context product recs, peak times around 3pm-5pm ET. P95 is okay but P99 jumps, sometimes spikes to 2.5s which causes retries in our gateway.
[00:43] Ava: got it, thanks. sounds like batching and KV cache might help; also wanted to check whether you're on hosted or dedicated for those endpoints?
[00:50] Tom: currently hosted for most, we started a small dedicated pool for high-volume flows but haven't moved the rec engine yet. cost has been the blocker to expand dedicated.
[01:02] Raj: also, curious about quantization recommendations - we run mix of Llama-2 variants and one open-source fine-tuned model. some folks on infra worry about accuracy regressions.
[01:15] Diego: for those models we can recommend 4-bit quant profiles and run evals on your regression test set; typical drop is small but depends on prompt distribution. we can run canary with A/B to measure.
[01:28] Ava: action: Diego will run a perf bench with your 2k token prompt set, compare hosted vs dedicated with and without quantization. we'll share the configs.
[01:35] Raj: ok that sounds good. question - in the spike on Oct 14 we had a region fallback to eu-west which increased latency. can we pin regional routing?
[01:47] Diego: yes, routing policies can be set by region and customer tier; however if capacity runs out we have automated fallback which you can configure to a cheaper variant or queue. we can also reserve burst capacity in Dedicated to avoid fallback.
[02:02] Mariana: what about data residency and logs - our security folks asked about audit trails and KMS integration for private deployment.
[02:10] Ava: Redwood Private offers VPC options + KMS/HSM integrations; we have SOC 2 report and an audit log export we can share. I'll attach the security pack after this call.
[02:20] Tom: perfect. on SLA, our product team wants a 99.9% availability objective for the rec endpoints and a P95 latency of under 300ms for short prompts, but we know long prompts are tougher.
[02:33] Diego: can you confirm expected QPS during peak? that helps sizing dedicated pools.
[02:37] Raj: expected peak is 140 qps for recs, but bursty; 95% of traffic short prompts, 5% long.
[02:45] Diego: ok, with that we can model batch sizes and estimate GPU need; also prefix/KV cache will reduce work for repeated sessions.
[02:55] Ava: about costs, we noticed their token spend rose 38% month-over-month; suggest caching and lowering max tokens for interactive flows, and offloading embeddings to cheaper model for low-criticality features.
[03:08] Mariana: embeddings cost is big for search indexing, do you have recommendations for batching?
[03:12] Diego: yes, we can batch embeddings and use semi-dedicated workers; batching window of 200-500ms usually yields big savings. we'll provide recommended batch/window for your traffic profile.
[03:24] Raj: any concerns on quality with quantization and batch? product team's worried about regression on top N recs.
[03:31] Diego: we'll run your eval suite, and use Redwood Optimize to suggest the model/quant profile. also, canary rollouts let you route small % to quantized variant to measure CTR changes.
[03:45] Tom: ok can we get a 1-pager of recommended changes and expected cost delta?
[03:50] Ava: yes - I'll include baseline cost, recommended config changes (batching, caching, quant profiles), and expected savings range.
[03:58] Raj: about the dedicated pool - what's the contract/commit look like? we might want a 6 month commit for predictable capacity.
[04:06] Ava: Dedicated has monthly and annual commits; we can put together a proposal for a 6 month reserve and include burst credits for holiday. pricing detail will be in the doc.
[04:15] Mariana: small note - our infra team uses their own KMS and wants to ensure no key material leaves our VPC. is that supported?
[04:22] Diego: yes, with Private we support customer-managed KMS and on-prem options; for hosted we offer envelope encryption backed by Redwood KMS, but Private keeps keys customer-side.
[04:33] Raj: great. any blockers on starting the perf run? we can provide the prompt set and test harness.
[04:38] Diego: send the prompt set to me (diego@redwood.ai) and I'll provision the slot. note: logs may have imperfect labels in our run, sorry about that, but we'll include full metrics.
[04:48] Ava: recap - Diego runs perf bench (hosted vs dedicated, quant tests), Ava sends usage & cost breakdown + security pack, Raj confirms SLA targets and peak windows, schedule follow-up week of Nov 15 for routing deep dive.
[04:58] Tom: thanks all.
[05:00] Ava: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite and docs. bye.
